content.intro: This lesson covers Dereferencing Raw Pointers. It sits in Module 20, Unsafe Rust and Foreign Function Interfaces, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Dereferencing Raw Pointers matters when you work with unsafe invariants and external contracts. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Unsafe Rust permits a narrow set of operations whose safety obligations the compiler cannot fully prove. Every unsafe boundary needs explicit invariants, valid initialization, correct aliasing, and compatible external contracts.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
